findings.obs_text: In 1Ti 6:5 gain is the content of the false view: people depraved in mind imagine that godliness is a means of gain.
findings.grounds: godliness is a means of gain

findings.obs_text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews who were consoling Mary in the house follow her out, supposing she goes to the tomb: the consoling is what they were doing when the supposing moved them.
findings.grounds: consoling her, saw Mary rise quickly

findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 13:32 command is the word of Absalom by which the deed was set: Jonadab corrects the king's view by naming that the killing was by Absalom's command, from the day Tamar was violated. The pairing with command is through the code of saying (H0559) behind suppose.

In Luk 7:43 Simon gives his view and Jesus says he has judged rightly: the supposing is weighed and found correct. In Rom 2:3 the one who judges others is asked whether he supposes he will escape: judging others stands against a false view of oneself.

older.reason: it states how condemn works in a person; the condemn collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Act 14:19 the crowds, persuaded by the Jews from Antioch and Iconium, stone Paul and drag him out, supposing him dead: the persuading moves them to the act, and the supposing ends it.
In 2Sa 13:32 violated names the wrong done to Tamar, the cause Jonadab gives for Amnon's death against the king's fear that all his sons are dead.
findings.grounds: the day he violated his sister Tamar

findings.obs_text: In 2Sa 13:32 determined names Absalom's purpose held since Tamar was violated: Jonadab sets this settled intent against the king's view.
In Joh 11:31 going is the content of the supposing: the Jews take Mary to be going to the tomb to weep there.
findings.grounds: she was going to the tomb

findings.obs_text: In Jam 4:5 the readers are asked whether they suppose the Scripture speaks to no purpose, and what it says is that he yearns jealously over the spirit: the question presses them to take the yearning seriously.
findings.grounds: He yearns jealously over the spirit

older.finding: God's jealous yearning over the spirit: "He yearns jealously over the spirit that he has made to dwell in us" (Jam 4:5) [U] — the classification leaves open whether this is the human spirit or God's.
older.reason: it states how desire works in a person; the desire collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Gen 18:28, Gen 18:31 and Gen 18:32 each case Abraham puts with suppose is answered on destroying: will you destroy the city, and the Lord says he will not destroy it for the sake of the number. The case is put to hold back destruction.
findings.grounds: For the sake of ten I will not destroy it

findings.obs_text: In Act 16:27 the jailer supposes the prisoners have escaped and is about to kill himself: the false view nearly leads to his death. In Rom 2:3 the man who judges is asked if he supposes he will escape God's judgment: escape is the content of a false view in both.
findings.grounds: supposing that the prisoners had escaped

findings.obs_text: In 1Ti 6:5 those who imagine godliness is gain have a corrupted mind and have lost the truth: the false view is set in a depraved mind.
findings.grounds: depraved in mind and deprived of the truth

findings.obs_text: In Joh 11:31 the Jews followed Mary because of what they supposed: the following is the act that rests on the supposing.
